artifact.canonical_name: Enhancing Automotive User Experience with Dynamic Service Orchestration for Software Defined Vehicles

sources.title: Enhancing Automotive User Experience with Dynamic Service Orchestration for Software Defined Vehicles
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors propose a dynamic onboard service-orchestration algorithm that reacts to in-vehicle/V2X network health and onboard resource constraints by selecting degraded application modes to maximize user experience.
The work introduces Automotive eXperience Integrity Level (AXIL) as a runtime priority concept for non-safety-critical applications.
The authors report near-optimal solutions with substantially shorter execution time than straightforward methods in simulation.
claims.context: Abstract-level performance claim; detailed simulation conditions not verified.

limitations.text: The primary abstract does not expose enough detail to reconstruct scenario size, baselines, compute hardware, objective normalization, or runtime distributions.
A subsequent 2024 paper by the same authors presents dedicated test-bench validation, making this initial simulation study less suitable as the main empirical evidence for industrial feasibility.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Enhancing Automotive User Experience with Dynamic Service Orchestration for Software Defined Vehicles; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The v2 primary page verifies the algorithm, AXIL concept and simulation-level claim, but not the detailed evaluation setup needed to assess performance generality.

editorial.why_now_note: It illustrates runtime orchestration becoming an onboard architectural responsibility as SDV services and resource conditions become dynamic.
editorial.rationale: The orchestration concept is relevant to runtime resource governance, but the later experimental-validation paper is the stronger evidence item and this pass did not reconstruct the simulation setup.
